title: Vegan Earl Grey Tea Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft vegan cupcakes made with Earl Grey tea steeped in oat milk, ready in about 45 minutes with a 15 minute steep.
description: These cupcakes get their flavor from Earl Grey tea steeped right in warm oat milk. The tea gives the crumb a soft citrus and bergamot note without any eggs or dairy. I tested this batch three times in my own kitchen to get the crumb tender, not gummy. The trick is letting the tea milk cool before you mix it into the batter You can frost these plain with vanilla buttercream, or swirl in a little lavender for a floral twist. Both versions disappeared fast when I brought them to a book club meeting. This is a good beginner vegan recipe. No egg replacers to hunt down, just pantry staples and one tea bag.
ingredients: 1/3 cup neutral oil, such as canola
2 cups vegan powdered sugar, for frosting
1/2 cup vegan butter, softened, for frosting
1/4 tsp dried culinary lavender, finely ground, optional
instructions: Heat oat milk in a small pot until steaming, not boiling.
Remove from heat, add tea bags, and steep for 15 minutes. Squeeze bags out, then cool the tea milk fully.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin pan with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk cooled tea milk, oil, vanilla, and vinegar until combined.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir just until no dry streaks remain.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat vegan butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar gradually with vanilla.
If using lavender, fold ground lavender into half the frosting to create a swirl before piping onto cooled cupcakes.
tips: Cool the tea milk to room temperature before mixing. Warm milk can melt the oil too fast and change the texture.
Squeeze the tea bags well. This pulls out more bergamot flavor without adding bitterness.
Go light on lavender. A little goes a long way and too much tastes like soap.
For a stronger tea taste, steep one extra tea bag or steep for 20 minutes instead of 15.

faq.question: Can I use a different plant milk for these Earl Grey cupcakes?
faq.answer: Yes, soy milk or almond milk both work well. Oat milk gives the softest crumb because of its natural fat content.

faq.question: Why does my tea milk taste bitter?
faq.answer: Bitterness usually comes from steeping too long or squeezing the tea bags too hard. Stick to 15 minutes and a gentle squeeze.

faq.question: Can I skip the lavender in the frosting?
faq.answer: Yes, plain vanilla frosting works great here. The lavender swirl is optional and just adds a floral note.

faq.question: How do I store leftover Earl Grey cupcakes?
faq.answer: Keep them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerate for up to 5 days.

conclusion: These Earl Grey cupcakes are a simple way to bring a tea shop flavor into a vegan bake. Steep the tea, keep the frosting light, and you have a batch that works for everyday snacking or a small gathering.
